correctness.rationale: For any positive homogeneous Bernoulli retention rate, a parent atom above n would put positive thinned mass above n, so the inverse polynomial is forced. Its penultimate coefficient changes sign at the beta moment ratio r=(a+n-1)/(a+b+n-1). Independently, put k=n-j and I_j=integral_0^1 x^(a+j-1)(1-x)^(b-1)(r-x)^(n-j) dx. Integrate the derivative of x^(a+j)(1-x)^b(r-x)^(k-1); all endpoint terms vanish for positive a,b. Using (a+j)(1-r)-br=-(k-1)(1-r) gives (a+j)I_j=(k-1)[(2-r)I_(j+1)+(1-r)I_(j+2)] for k>=2, and I_(n-1)=0. The binomial prefactors of the inverse coefficients give exactly the stated recurrence. Strict positivity starts at indices n and n-2 and descends; normalization is Q(1)=1, and composition gives the admissible interval. For n=1 the unique boundary parent is constant 1. Dividing the top parent atom by the top child atom gives r^(-n), with -n log r tending to b. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed; its 162 rational cases are only a replay, not the proof.
